decision_description: Constitutional compliance check on docs/tier5_deliverables/review_packets/review_packet.json (schema_id: orch.tier5.review_packet.v1) identified three simultaneous critical violations sharing a single structural root cause — the review packet schema does not define a traceability_footer field, making per-claim traceability structurally impossible. (1) §13.2 violation: the artifact asserts MSCA-PF evaluation criterion weights (50%, 30%) and named sub-criterion requirements ('soundness of methodology', 'supervision and two-way transfer', 'Impact sub-criterion 2', weight designations in F-001, F-003, F-004) without any traceability_footer.primary_sources[] references to docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/ or any named Tier 2A/2B source document. (2) §13.3 violation: the artifact names specific consortium partners (AgroVIR, Eötvös Loránd University/ELTE), external companies (Cubert GmbH, Brightic Research), project personnel (Dr. András Jung), work packages (WP3, WP4, WP5), tasks (T4-01, T4-02), milestones (MS4, MS6), and deliverables (D4-01, D5-02) without traceability_footer.primary_sources[] references to docs/tier3_project_instantiation/. (3) §13.10 violation: the Tier 5 artifact contains no traceability_footer field, no no_unsupported_claims_declaration, and no source_refs for any claim across its five findings and five revision actions — making it structurally impossible to satisfy §13.10 per-claim traceability requirements. The violations are assessed as plausibly-grounded-but-constitutionally-non-compliant: the project facts and evaluation criteria referenced in the review packet are consistent with other Tier 3 and Tier 2A/2B artifacts present in the repository, but the traceability chain is not documented in the artifact structure. Resolution requires human operator determination of one of two paths: (a) schema amendment — the orch.tier5.review_packet.v1 schema in artifact_schema_specification.yaml must be amended to require a traceability_footer field with source_refs for each finding's evidence basis; or (b) formal exception — second-order audit/review artifacts that audit first-order Tier 5 artifacts (which themselves carry traceability_footer) are formally exempt from per-claim §13.2, §13.3, §13.10 traceability by a schema-level exception, which must be registered in artifact_schema_specification.yaml and recorded as a constitutional decision log entry per CLAUDE.md §14.5.
alternatives_considered: Record the three violations as three separate decision log entries (one per §13.x prohibition) — rejected in favour of a single consolidated entry because all three violations share the same structural root cause (missing schema-level traceability_footer in orch.tier5.review_packet.v1); separating them would obscure the single-point schema deficiency requiring resolution and produce redundant resolution paths.

Classify all three violations as resolved on the grounds that the constitutional-compliance-check report (docs/tier4_orchestration_state/validation_reports/constitutional-compliance-check_msca-pf-.json) already documents them with embedded decision_log_entries — rejected per CLAUDE.md §9.4 and §13.5: embedded entries in a validation report artifact do not constitute durable decision log entries in docs/tier4_orchestration_state/decision_log/; the violations remain unresolved until a human operator determines the resolution path, which exceeds automated orchestration authority.

Classify as a tier_conflict_resolution between the orch.tier5.review_packet.v1 schema definition and §13.10 traceability requirements — rejected because this is a constitutional violation (the schema does not satisfy constitutional requirements), not a conflict between two equally-authoritative tier sources; the constitution governs unconditionally per CLAUDE.md §15.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §13.10; §13.2; §13.3 — Tier 5 outputs must be traceable to specific inputs in Tier 1–4; no call constraints or expected outcomes may be asserted without source_refs to named Tier 2B documents; no project facts may be asserted without source_refs to named Tier 3 documents
rationale: The compliance validator executed a §13 prohibition check against the review packet artifact and confirmed three critical violations, all attributable to the absence of a traceability_footer field in the orch.tier5.review_packet.v1 schema. The violations are structural, not epistemological: the underlying data — MSCA-PF evaluation criterion weights, partner identities, WP effort allocations, milestone criteria — appears consistent with Tier 2A/2B and Tier 3 artifacts visible in other phase outputs and assembled draft consistency checks. However, CLAUDE.md §13.10 requires that Tier 5 outputs be traceable to specific named Tier 1–4 inputs within the artifact structure; §13.2 and §13.3 require source_refs to the specific named documents. The review packet schema provides no mechanism for carrying this traceability. This decision is recorded as unresolved because the resolution requires either a schema-level amendment or a formal constitutional exception — both requiring explicit human operator instruction per CLAUDE.md §14.5 (constitutional amendments may not be made by agents operating autonomously). The consolidated entry satisfies CLAUDE.md §9.4 (decisions affecting future interpretation must be written to the decision log) and §12.3 (contradictions between artifact structure and constitutional requirements must be resolved explicitly with the resolution method recorded).
